title: PCIe Enumeration
description: Walks the PCIe config space discovering devices, bridges, and their BARs. The enumerator assigns bus numbers depth-first and maps memory windows. Every PCIe device in the system is found this way at boot.

demo.title: Demo — PCIe Enumeration

title: I2C Transactions
description: Performs addressed transactions on the two-wire I2C bus with start, address, ACK, and stop. Clock stretching lets slow slaves hold the clock; 7-bit addressing picks the device. Sensors and EEPROMs live on I2C.
key_mechanisms: Issue stop to release the bus

demo.title: Demo — I2C Transactions

title: SPI Transfers
description: Shifts data full-duplex over SPI with chip-select framing and four clock modes. Mode (CPOL/CPHA) must match the slave; speed is limited by signal integrity. Flash chips and displays use SPI.

demo.title: Demo — SPI Transfers

title: UART Communication
description: Exchanges bytes over UART with agreed baud rate, parity, and stop bits. No clock line means both sides must agree on timing; framing errors reveal mismatches. Consoles and GPS modules still speak UART.

demo.title: Demo — UART Communication

title: CAN Bus Messaging
description: Broadcasts prioritized frames on CAN with non-destructive arbitration. Lower IDs win the bus without corruption; error frames isolate faulty nodes. Cars and industrial gear run on CAN.

demo.title: Demo — CAN Bus Messaging

title: GPIO Control
description: Drives general-purpose I/O pins for LEDs, resets, and bit-banged protocols. Direction, pull-ups, and drive strength are configured per pin; interrupts catch edges. It is the simplest hardware interface there is.

demo.title: Demo — GPIO Control

title: MMIO vs PIO Access
description: Chooses memory-mapped I/O over port I/O for device registers. MMIO maps registers into address space for normal loads and stores; x86 PIO uses special instructions. Modern drivers use MMIO almost exclusively.
key_mechanisms: Map BARs into virtual address space

demo.title: Demo — MMIO vs PIO Access

title: MSI-X Interrupts
description: Delivers per-queue interrupts with MSI-X message-signaled interrupts. Each queue gets its own vector and CPU affinity, eliminating IRQ sharing. High-performance NICs and NVMe depend on it.

demo.title: Demo — MSI-X Interrupts

title: DMA Engine Programming
description: Programs DMA engines with descriptor rings for CPU-free data movement. The driver builds descriptors, rings the doorbell, and handles completions; cache coherency is managed explicitly. It is how fast I/O avoids the CPU.

demo.title: Demo — DMA Engine Programming

title: Bus Enumeration Order
description: Enumerates buses in dependency order so bridges come up before their devices. Depth-first assignment gives stable bus numbers; hot-plug slots get reserved ranges. Order matters for correct resource assignment.

demo.title: Demo — Bus Enumeration Order

title: BAR Mapping
description: Maps Base Address Registers into the CPU address space with correct caching attributes. Sizing probes reveal each BAR's size; prefetchable 64-bit BARs go high. Wrong attributes cause subtle corruption.
key_mechanisms: Size BARs by writing all ones

demo.title: Demo — BAR Mapping

title: Clock Stretching Handling
description: Handles I2C clock stretching where slow slaves hold SCL low. Masters must wait rather than time out; multi-master arbitration adds complexity. Robust drivers never assume the clock is theirs.

demo.title: Demo — Clock Stretching Handling

title: Bus Analyzer Tracing
description: Captures bus traffic with protocol analyzers to debug driver issues. Seeing the actual bytes settles every argument about who is wrong. Analyzers decode PCIe, I2C, SPI, and CAN natively.

demo.title: Demo — Bus Analyzer Tracing

title: SMBus Communication
description: Uses SMBus, the I2C subset, for system management like battery and thermal data. Strict timeouts and protocols like Block Write make it more robust than raw I2C. Smart batteries speak SMBus.

demo.title: Demo — SMBus Communication

title: LPC Bus Bridging
description: Bridges the legacy Low Pin Count bus for super-I/O and TPM on older platforms. eSPI replaces it on modern boards, but millions of systems still boot through LPC. The bridge translates to modern fabrics internally.

demo.title: Demo — LPC Bus Bridging
